title: lifedraft input contract — universal $defs: the cash_flows[], household_budget, installments[], equity_grants[] and gifts[] blocks
$comment: Fragment of the universal input contract, merged into schema/input_schema.json by input_contract.load_universal_schema() -- see that function and compose_schema() for the exact, total merge rule. This file is a FRAGMENT, not a standalone schema: its "#/$defs/..." references resolve only in the composed document. Money moving through the year that is neither an owned account nor a debt: declared cash flows, the measured household budget and its expense segments, fixed-term installment obligations, record-only equity grants and their vesting, and parent-to-child gifts.

zev_purchase.description: One dated zero-emission vehicle acquisition. Every field here is a term a government program TESTS -- DP#7: no field names a make or a model, because no statute does. The federal and provincial programs are independent: a household may receive both, one, or neither, and each reports its own reasons when it pays nothing (DP#32).

acquisition_date.description: The date the vehicle was registered. DP#1: the ACTUAL date, never a year -- both programs have eligibility edges that fall mid-year (the iZEV pause on 2025-01-12 and close on 2025-03-31; the Roulez vert suspension from 2025-02-01 to 2025-03-31), so a year alone cannot resolve eligibility.

base_msrp.description: MSRP of the model's BASE trim, in dollars. iZEV caps the base trim (< $55,000 for a car, < $60,000 for a larger vehicle); a model whose base trim is over its cap is ineligible in EVERY trim, so this cannot be inferred from what was actually paid.

trim_msrp.description: MSRP of the trim actually acquired, in dollars. Tested against the higher-trim iZEV ceiling ($65,000 car / $70,000 larger) and against the $65,000 Roulez vert cap. Must be >= base_msrp.

vehicle_class.description: The statutory iZEV class that selects the MSRP caps: 'car', or 'larger' for an SUV, van or truck. A marketing segment is not a class (DP#7).

propulsion.description: Propulsion type, which selects the federal amount and gates the Quebec one. Quebec's new-vehicle rebate is priced here ONLY for battery_electric; hydrogen and phev are refused BY NAME rather than paid the battery-electric amount.

electric_range_km.description: Electric-only range in km. REQUIRED for a phev, where it selects between the $5,000 and $2,500 federal amount at a 50 km threshold and therefore cannot be defaulted (DP#32). Ignored for battery_electric and hydrogen.

is_lease.description: Whether the vehicle was leased rather than purchased. A lease prorates the federal incentive by term.

lease_term_months.description: Lease term in months. REQUIRED when is_lease is true: it prorates the federal incentive (full at 48 months or longer, otherwise term/48) and cannot be inferred.

owner.description: null = household-level (not attributable to one person).

date.description: Replaces the old `.year` integer (#594) — a date, per DP#1.

annual_living_costs.description: Issue #679: the household's own measured annual working-phase spend outside any account or debt payment (housing/utilities/food/transport/etc. -- NOT the mortgage payment, which is already on liabilities[kind=mortgage], and NOT the retirement assumptions.retirement.spending_target, which only applies post-retirement). null = not measured; the cash-flow solvency invariant does not run without it (DP#16). A household that declares this omits the input entirely rather than writing 0 -- no real household spends nothing to live.

x-uncertainty.resolved_by: Your own budget: 12 months of bank/credit statements — total spend, minus debt payments and minus savings/investment contributions.
x-uncertainty.question: What does this household actually spend per year to live, outside its mortgage payment and its own savings?

discretionary_fraction.description: Issue #761: the fraction (0..1) of annual_living_costs that is DISCRETIONARY -- restaurants, alcohol, vacations, entertainment: spending a household cuts FIRST under an income shock. The remainder (1 - fraction) is NON-DISCRETIONARY (groceries, utilities, insurance, phones, transport, medicine) and stays rigid, alongside debt service and any committed installment (#759). Optional and deliberately NOT required (DP#16): omitting it reproduces today's behaviour exactly -- the solvency/runway identity treats the WHOLE scalar as rigid, and the output says so explicitly (the runway_treats_all_spend_as_rigid approximation fires), never inventing a fraction (DP#32). Under a dated income shock (decisions.income[] with an override that reduces income below baseline), the runway/solvency identity compresses the discretionary portion to ZERO -- a labelled, documented stress assumption (a household in genuine distress stops dining out and taking vacations; it does not stop buying groceries or paying insurance). 0.0 = all rigid (explicit); 1.0 = all discretionary (explicit); both are real declarable values, distinct from omitting the field.

expense_segments.description: Issue #760: dated, finite-term living-cost segments ON TOP OF the perpetual annual_living_costs scalar -- a private-school tuition that ENDS when a child ages out, childcare that ages out, a term expense that stops on a date. The scalar can only smear such a cost across the whole horizon (carrying a child's tuition through retirement and into the estate -- wrong, and wrong in the direction that makes the household look poorer than it is). Each segment is an ANNUAL recurring amount active over [from, to): it contributes its amount prorated by the days of that window falling in each calendar year (day-count blend, the outflow-side analog of #674's dated income windows), and a non-null `to` means the expense STOPS after that date (reverts to $0, never carried to the horizon). Optional and deliberately NOT required (DP#16): omitting it reproduces today's behaviour exactly (the golden invariant does not move, DP#32). Each segment folds into the solvency identity's spending outflow (simulation_rules.apply_solvency) beside annual_living_costs; a discretionary segment (non_discretionary=false) compresses to zero under an income shock exactly as #761's scalar split does, a non-discretionary one stays rigid. Requires annual_living_costs to be declared -- a dated segment WITHOUT the measured base fails loudly at the contract boundary (DP#32), never defaulting the base to zero.

expense_segment.$comment: Issue #760. A dated, finite-term living-cost segment layered ON TOP of the perpetual household_budget.annual_living_costs scalar -- a private-school tuition that ends when a child ages out, childcare, a term expense that stops. `amount` is an ANNUAL recurring figure; the segment is active over the half-open window [from, to) and contributes `amount` prorated by the days of that window falling in each calendar year (day-count blend, the outflow-side analog of #674's dated income segments). `to` is REQUIRED and nullable: null is the EXPLICIT spelling of 'perpetual / no known end' (DP#32 -- an open-ended segment must SAY null, not omit the key), a non-null date means the expense ENDS there and contributes $0 afterwards (never carried to the horizon the way the base scalar is). `non_discretionary` is REQUIRED: true = a committed, must-pay dated expense that stays rigid under an income shock (tuition, childcare); false = a dated discretionary expense that compresses to $0 under a dated income shock exactly as #761's scalar discretionary split does. The two values are genuinely distinct decisions, so neither may be defaulted (DP#32 two-way trap). A segment can only be declared alongside a measured annual_living_costs -- the base engages the solvency module (DP#16); a segment without it is refused at load.

description.description: What the segment pays for (e.g. 'private-school tuition, child_a', 'daycare'). A FACT, free text.

amount.description: The ANNUAL recurring amount while the segment is active (same annual convention as annual_living_costs). Prorated by the days of [from, to) that fall in each calendar year, so a segment starting mid-year contributes a partial first year.

from.description: The date the segment starts (inclusive). May be before the document's as_of -- a living cost already underway at the snapshot (e.g. tuition begun last year) simply applies from the start of the projection; unlike an installment plan (#759) there is no already-paid lump to re-price, so a past `from` is honest, not refused.

to.description: The date the segment ENDS (exclusive), or null for perpetual. Required and nullable: null is the explicit DP#32 spelling of 'no known end' (an open-ended segment must declare null, never omit the key); a non-null date means the expense stops -- it contributes $0 from that date on, never carried to the horizon the way annual_living_costs is. Must be strictly after `from` (a zero/negative window is refused at load, not silently treated as $0).

non_discretionary.description: true = a committed, must-pay dated expense that does NOT compress under an income shock (tuition, childcare, insurance); false = a dated DISCRETIONARY expense that compresses to $0 under a dated income shock, exactly as #761's scalar discretionary split does. Both values are genuine, distinct decisions -- neither is defaulted (DP#32 two-way trap: silently treating a discretionary segment as rigid, or vice versa, is the exact defect the flag prevents).

active_months.$comment: Issue #882. OPTIONAL intra-year seasonality. Absent = the segment is active every day of its [from, to) window (the #760 day-count blend, unchanged). Present = a subset of calendar-month numbers (1=January .. 12=December) the segment recurs in: the ANNUAL `amount` is spent in EQUAL shares across only these months, so a bill that runs a few months a year (heating Nov-Mar -> [1,2,3,11,12]) or a one-shot charge dated to one month (property tax each July -> [7]) is resolved at MONTHLY granularity. The within-year charge counts only the active months the [from, to) window touches (a boundary month the window enters/leaves mid-way prorates by its days), and the emergency reserve is sized on the PEAK active month rather than the annual average -- a concentrated seasonal bill demands a larger reserve. An empty list or a duplicated month is refused at load (DP#32): an empty within-year window is not silently 'every month' or $0, and a repeated month is not silently de-duplicated.
active_months.description: Optional calendar months (1-12) the segment's annual amount is spent in; absent = active year-round (#760 behaviour).

installment_plan.$comment: Issue #759. A fixed-term, zero-interest installment obligation -- the contract for a medical/dental/education payment plan that is neither a liability (no drawable facility, no collateral, no prepayment/refinance) nor a perpetual living cost. `start_date` is the date of the FIRST monthly payment and MUST be on or after the document's `as_of` (the up-front lump is already paid before the snapshot; the simulation models only the remaining N payments forward from `as_of`). The final payment date -- the end of the plan's finite term -- is DERIVED as `start_date + (number_of_payments - 1) months`; it is not declared separately, so the term cannot be stated two conflicting ways (DP#32: one spelling of the fact). `rate` is REQUIRED and must be 0: a 0%-interest plan is the whole point of this block, and a stated-rate plan's interest pricing/attribution is out of scope (#759) -- a non-zero `rate` is REFUSED at load rather than silently coerced to 0 or silently honoured. `non_discretionary` is REQUIRED and must be true: an installment plan is by construction a must-pay contractual outflow that does NOT compress under an income shock (contrast #761); a `false` value is refused loudly rather than silently treated as compressible. `final_payment` is the one optional field: omitted = no balloon (a structural absence, not a silent zero -- a $0 balloon is meaningless).

owner.description: The person(s) legally bound to the payment plan.

description.description: What the plan pays for (e.g. 'orthodontic payment plan', 'tuition installment plan'). A FACT, free text.

start_date.description: The date of the FIRST monthly payment. Must be on or after the document's as_of (the up-front lump is already paid; the simulation models only the remaining installments forward).

monthly_amount.description: Each of the N equal monthly payments.

number_of_payments.description: The count of equal monthly payments. The final payment date is start_date + (number_of_payments - 1) months.

final_payment.description: Optional balloon payment made on the same date as the last monthly payment (start_date + number_of_payments - 1 months). Omitted = no balloon.

rate.description: The annual interest rate as a fraction. REQUIRED and must be 0: this block models a 0%-interest plan; a stated-rate plan's interest pricing is out of scope (#759) and a non-zero value is refused at load (DP#32).

non_discretionary.description: Required and must be true: an installment plan is a must-pay contractual outflow that does not compress under an income shock (contrast #761's discretionary split). A false value is refused at load rather than silently treated as compressible (DP#32).

equity_grant.$comment: Issue #768. A private-company stock-option / equity grant the household holds. This is a RECORD, not an asset: the engine values it at $0 for every solvency / runway / decumulation metric and never counts it as a liquid resource, because a private, unvested, or strike-undetermined option cannot be sold and realises only on a speculative liquidity event outside the projection. `strike` is nullable: null means 'not yet set / TBD' -- the option has no determinable value today, and the engine must say so (output 'strike TBD') rather than invent one (DP#32). `liquidity` is 'private' for a grant on a company with no public market (the case this block exists for) or 'public' for one with a listed market (still recorded, still $0 here until a dated liquidity event is modelled -- a separate, speculative input not in this block).

owner.description: The person who holds the grant (the optionee).

grantor.description: The company granting the options (the issuer). A FACT, free text -- a branded company name is fine here because it is the user's own document, not library code (DP#7 is about engine modelling, not about what a user writes in their input).

grant_date.description: The date the grant was made (the board/compensation-committee grant date).

vesting.description: The vesting schedule: a cliff date (0% vests before it -- termination before the cliff forfeits everything) and the date 100% vests.

strike.description: The per-share exercise/strike price. null = not yet set (TBD): the option has no determinable value today and the engine surfaces 'strike TBD' (DP#32: never invent a value).

liquidity.description: private = the grant is on a company with no public market (cannot be sold); public = a listed market exists. Both are recorded at $0 here until an explicitly-modelled, dated liquidity event (a separate, speculative input) -- this block is record-only.

shares.description: The number of options/shares in the grant. Optional -- a record of the size, not used to value the grant (no market price to multiply by).

fully_diluted_pct.description: The grant's share of the company on a fully-diluted basis. Optional record; not used to value the grant.

notes.description: Free-text notes (e.g. 'exercisable for 7 years after vesting', 'subject to acceleration on change of control'). A FACT about the grant's terms.

equity_vesting.$comment: Issue #768. The vesting schedule of an equity grant. `cliff_date` is the first date ANY shares vest (termination before it forfeits the entire grant -- 0% vests); `fully_vested_date` is the date 100% vests. The interim schedule (monthly/quarterly instalments between the cliff and full vesting) is free-text `schedule` -- it does not change the $0-for-solvency valuation (the grant is $0 regardless of vesting state until a dated liquidity event), so it is a record, not a rule input.

cliff_date.description: The first date any shares vest. Termination before this date forfeits the entire grant (0% vested).

fully_vested_date.description: The date 100% of the grant is vested.

schedule.description: Free-text description of the interim vesting (e.g. '25% at the 1-year cliff, then 1/36 monthly thereafter'). A record; the engine does not value partial vesting (the grant stays $0 until a dated liquidity event).

gift.description: Epic #841 bite 3: a parent->child cash gift that funds the child's OWN registered contributions. Redirects after-tax savings from the household adult base to the child's registered room (DP#18: conserved). Tax-free to both (not income to the child, not deductible to the donor). Applied each projection year, self-limited by the child's remaining registered room (never funds non-registered).

id.description: Epic #841 bite 3: stable identifier for this gift.

from.description: Epic #841 bite 3: the DONOR -- a declared adult household member whose after-tax savings base funds the gift. Must resolve to a declared member (DP#32: an unresolvable reference is refused loudly, not a zero gift).

to.description: Epic #841 bite 3: the RECIPIENT -- a declared child of the household whose OWN registered room the gift fills. Must resolve to a declared child (DP#32: a gift to a non-child or an undeclared person is refused loudly).

amount.description: Epic #841 bite 3: the annual cash gift. Funds the child's registered contribution up to the child's remaining registered room this year; the excess is not transferred (self-limiting -- the donor keeps what the room cannot absorb).

repayable.description: Issue #859 (Part A): when true, this transfer is an intra-family LOAN rather than a gift. It funds the child's registered room IDENTICALLY (same room cap, same #857 accrual), but the principal that lands is booked on the FAMILY BALANCE SHEET as a RECEIVABLE the donor keeps (asset) and a LIABILITY the child owes -- so a funding loan does NOT reduce the lender's net worth (DP#18: the receivable offsets the carve), unlike a gift given away. The family TOTAL is unchanged (an intra-family loan is a wash: receivable == liability). Absent/false = a plain gift (given away).

transaction_cost_event.description: Issue #139: the financial event this one-time cost or credit attaches to. "refinance_origination" = the closing costs/credits of a cash-out refinance (discharge/quittance, notary/legal, title insurance, appraisal, lender credit); a LUMP (no installments) of these reduces the refinance cash-out's deployable principal so NET proceeds are what deploys (the same year-0-equivalent reduction seam #137's deployment-lag carry uses). "account_transfer_in" = the economics of transferring an account INTO the household (a transfer-out fee, a reimbursement credit, a match-bonus credit optionally paid over an installment schedule); these flow as dated cash flows. The set of attachment points is a closed enum -- a new event is a real modelling decision (where the cost/credit deploys), not a free string (DP#32).

transaction_cost_installments.description: Issue #139: an OPTIONAL installment schedule. When present, the amount is paid in N EQUAL monthly payments starting at the entry's dated point (its `date`, or the document's `as_of` when `anchor` is "year_0") -- an installment is NOT a year-0 lump: the payments are aggregated into calendar years and flow as dated cash flows, so a match bonus paid over 12 months projects to a DIFFERENT trajectory than the same bonus paid as a year-0 lump (less year-0 compounding). When absent, the whole amount is a single lump at the dated point. A month count <= 0 is refused by the schema (minimum 1); the adapter aggregates the months into calendar years from the start date (DP#1: the actual dates, never a coarser year).

months.description: The number of EQUAL monthly payments the amount is split into. The monthly amount is amount / months; payments are aggregated into calendar years from the entry's start date (its `date`, or the document's `as_of` when `anchor` is "year_0"). A 12-month schedule starting mid-year-0 thus spans two calendar years, and an 18-month schedule spans three -- producing a genuinely different trajectory from a year-0 lump.

transaction_cost.description: Issue #139: one declarable one-time transaction cost or credit attached to a financial event -- the general mechanism the engine previously had only two ad-hoc members of (a property sale's selling_costs and a mortgage's cash_back origination credit, #1075). Exactly one of `date` or `anchor` is required (enforced by the oneOf below): `date` is the actual calendar date the cost/credit is paid (DP#1); `anchor` is an event-relative anchor ('year_0' = the document's as_of, the start of the projection) for a cost/credit that attaches to a year-0 event whose exact date the household has not stated. `amount` is a NON-NEGATIVE money magnitude (the direction field carries the sign); a negative amount is refused by the schema (minimum 0) AND by the adapter. `direction` is a closed enum (cost | credit) -- an unknown value is refused at schema validation AND by the adapter (DP#32 two-way: never silently coerce an unknown direction to the favourable value). `tax_treatment` is an optional enum (non_taxable | post_tax, default non_taxable) carrying the rebate-vs-bonus distinction: a credit that is a REBATE/reimbursement (a lender credit, a transfer-fee reimbursement) is non_taxable -- NOT income, flows as a non-taxable savings cash flow (the same treatment the mortgage cash_back uses, #1075); a credit that is a TAXABLE bonus (a match bonus on an account transfer-in) is post_tax -- ordinary employment income, marked so the engine's cash-flow mechanism can distinguish it from a rebate (DP#27). A cost is always non_taxable (an expense is never income). The default (absent key) is non_taxable: a cost/credit is a rebate unless declared a bonus (DP#13: a default is a fallback for absent input, never an opinion that coerces a supplied value). `label` is an optional itemization string (e.g. 'notary', 'title insurance') so a household can itemize the components of one event's origination; it is a FACT, free text, never consumed by a rule. `installments` is an optional schedule that turns the amount into N equal monthly payments (see transaction_cost_installments) -- an installment is NOT a year-0 lump. A refinance_origination LUMP (no installments) reduces the refinance cash-out's deployable principal so NET proceeds are what deploys; a net CREDIT among year-0 refinance lumps is FLOORED at the deployable seam (max(net, 0.0)) so the deployable principal never exceeds the borrowed lump (DP#18 money conservation), and the excess credit is routed as a year-0 SAVINGS cash flow instead. A refinance_origination installment, and every account_transfer_in entry, flow as dated cash flows.

id.description: Stable identifier for this transaction cost/credit.

amount.description: The NON-NEGATIVE dollar magnitude of this cost or credit. The sign is carried by `direction` (cost = a reduction, credit = an addition); a negative amount is refused (DP#32). A declared 0 is a real value (a $0 cost/credit) and is honoured explicitly -- it round-trips and carries no effect, byte-identical to the no-op path.

direction.description: cost = a one-time charge that reduces net proceeds (a notary fee, a transfer-out fee); credit = a one-time addition that increases net proceeds (a lender credit, a reimbursement, a match bonus). An unknown value is refused by the schema's enum AND by the adapter (DP#32). A credit's tax treatment (rebate vs bonus) is carried by `tax_treatment`, not this field.

date.description: The actual calendar date this cost/credit is paid (DP#1). Must be on or after the document's `as_of` (a date before the snapshot is refused by the adapter, not silently dropped -- DP#32). Exactly one of `date` and `anchor` is required.

anchor.description: An event-relative anchor: 'year_0' = the document's `as_of` (the start of the projection), for a cost/credit that attaches to a year-0 event whose exact date the household has not stated (e.g. a refinance origination closing at the snapshot). Exactly one of `date` and `anchor` is required.

tax_treatment.description: Issue #139: the rebate-vs-bonus distinction for a CREDIT. `non_taxable` (the default) = a rebate/reimbursement -- a lender credit or a transfer-fee reimbursement, NOT income, flows as a non-taxable savings cash flow (the same treatment the mortgage cash_back uses, #1075). `post_tax` = a TAXABLE bonus -- a match bonus on an account transfer-in, ordinary employment income, marked so the engine's cash-flow mechanism can apply the rebate-vs-bonus distinction (DP#27). A cost is always non_taxable (an expense is never income). An unknown value is refused by the schema's enum AND by the adapter (DP#32 two-way). The default (absent key) is non_taxable: a cost/credit is a rebate unless declared a bonus (DP#13).

label.description: Optional itemization label (e.g. 'notary', 'title insurance', 'appraisal', 'discharge fee') so a household can itemize the components of one event's origination. A FACT, free text; never consumed by a rule.

installments.description: Optional installment schedule: split the amount into N equal monthly payments starting at the entry's dated point. When present, the amount is NOT a year-0 lump -- it flows as dated cash flows aggregated into calendar years, producing a different trajectory from the same amount paid as a lump. Absent = a single lump at the dated point.
